newsitem.title: USA: Broker test fraud alleged, arrests expected - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Broker test fraud alleged, arrests expected - WSJ.

text.p: Capping a two-and-a-half year investigation, state prosecutors are expected to announce the arrests of about 50 stock brokers suspected of having their broker-licensing examinations taken by stand-ins, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
The expected action by the Manhattan District Attorney's office would be the first time that officials have alleged widespread criminal fraud in brokerage test taking, the story said.
The investigation was initiated by an anonymous tip given to the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD), the newspaper reported.
The district attorney's office followed up on the tip by analyzing handwriting samples, and the investigation is continuing, the story said.
The district attorney's office and the NASD declined to comment for the Journal's story.
In civil actions, the NASD has censured 21 brokers since August and banned them from the securities business for allegedly paying people to stand in for them during the exams, the story says.
